title: Before You Send a Deposit: What Every Pet Scam Has in Common
body:
A message lands in your inbox or your WhatsApp: a beautiful puppy, a fair price, and one small catch, send a deposit first, because "so many people are interested." It is one of the oldest tricks in the pet world, and it still works, because it is built around a plausible-sounding urgency rather than an obvious lie.

The US Federal Trade Commission published a consumer alert this year walking through exactly this pattern: a seller who can't meet in person, a story about shipping or import fees, and pressure to pay before you've seen the animal, or the person, for yourself. None of that is unique to any one country. The shape of the scam travels well because it exploits the same thing everywhere, how hard it is to say no to a photo of a pet you already want.

Nigeria has its own version of the same story, usually playing out in WhatsApp groups and Facebook listings rather than classified ads. The details shift; the ask, money moving before anyone actually meets, does not.

It is also the exact reason PetMatch is built the way it is. Listing a pet or contacting another owner here never involves PetMatch handling money: no fees, no deposits, no "reservation" payments. A directory that never touches money can't be used to run that particular trick. That said, every listing on PetMatch is self-reported, not independently verified by us, so the same caution you'd use with any stranger online still applies, which is exactly why meeting in person matters more than any message thread.

Before anything else, meet the pet and the owner face to face, somewhere neutral if you can manage it, and ask to see health and vaccination records directly rather than taking a description on faith. If a conversation ever turns toward sending money before that meeting happens, that is the moment to stop, not the moment to trust harder.

None of this makes finding a pet, or a match for one, risk-free. It just means the real risk is smaller and more manageable than the version scammers are counting on you to imagine. More on how PetMatch approaches this is at https://petmatch.fit/safety.
